label: Dataset ID
description: Dataset specification identifier
missing_rule: Always populated from the dataset specification
notes: System variable injected during harmonisation

label: Dataset name
description: Dataset specification name
missing_rule: Always populated from the dataset specification
notes: System variable injected during harmonisation

label: Participant ID
description: Study-specific participant identifier
notes: Numeric ids: sprintf("%.0f", id). Same id across a participant's waves; unique within dataset x wave x st_measure_id. Ids that restart per survey: build <year>_<id> in the tidier. Rows keyed by row position or a row counter: inferred; name the affected waves.

label: Wave
description: Study wave or collection occasion
missing_rule: Use NA (row unavailable) when the supplied data hold a single collection occasion, even if the study labels it a wave of a longer study
notes: Panels: the study's own wave label as the spec or data carries it (T1, sweep_3, Year 9, 2016). Repeated cross-sections: four-digit survey year; add a sample suffix only when one year fielded separate samples (2015_sample_1). A second report on the same occasion is a tagged measure (st_measure_id), not a wave.

label: Year data were collected
description: Calendar year in which the row's data were collected
missing_rule: Where a per-row date is missing, use the wave's modal fieldwork year; NA only when no year can be assigned
notes: Per-row interview or visit year where released, from the component that asked the screen items (compatible). Otherwise the survey's own year label (compatible). A few missing per-row dates filled with the wave's modal fieldwork year leave the row compatible; give the count. A year assigned wholesale from wave labels or documentation is the modal fieldwork year, or the midpoint of a multi-year window (inferred). Cite fieldwork documentation, never a publication year.

label: RCT arm
description: Trial arm the participant was allocated to, for datasets from randomised controlled trials
missing_rule: Use NA if not applicable (i.e., not a randomised trial)
notes: Arm names from the trial's main outcome publication; Control for the control or usual-care arm. Arm given by a variable or by the provider's file or sheet split: compatible; decoded from undocumented codes (e.g. an id character): inferred. Not a trial: unavailable, note 'Not a randomised trial.' Covariate when pooling RCT cohorts (DR-0001).

label: Survey weight
description: Main participant weight for the wave, as released by the study
missing_rule: Use NA if the study releases no weight or is not a survey sample
notes: Cross-sectional participant weight for the wave, not rescaled. Where only longitudinal weights exist, map one and say which. Replicate weights are not harmonised. Use the study's core release weight; a design weight fixed at sampling may be carried within participant to later waves (partial).

label: Survey stratum
description: Sampling stratum used for variance estimation
missing_rule: Use NA if not released or not a survey sample
notes: Values fixed at sampling are carried within participant to every wave, without a wave prefix, so a participant stays in one stratum. Repeated cross-sections prefix codes with the wave where the study reuses them across waves.

label: Survey cluster
description: Primary sampling unit (usually the school or area) used for variance estimation
missing_rule: Use NA if not released or not a survey sample
notes: School ids qualify when schools were the sampled units; partial where the design is not documented. Schools in a randomised trial are not survey clusters. Values fixed at sampling are carried within participant to every wave, without a wave prefix, so a participant stays in one cluster. Repeated cross-sections prefix codes with the wave where the study reuses them across waves.

label: Age in years
description: Participant age at the observation in years
missing_rule: Use NA when age cannot be derived
notes: Decimal years at the observation. Dates, months / 12 or tenths: as is. Birth year and month with the interview month or a documented fieldwork midpoint: derive decimal age. Completed years: +0.5 (13 -> 13.5). Completed-year band a-b: (a + b + 1) / 2 (13-15 -> 14.5). Open band: inclusive bound + 0.5 (12 or younger -> 12.5; 18 or older -> 18.5). Survey year minus birth year: + (fieldwork midpoint as a fraction of the year - 0.5). No age item: centre of the sampled cohort's age at fieldwork, inferred. Keep values above max_value. Say in notes which kind the source is.

label: Sex
description: Participant sex or gender as recorded by the source
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Male and Female from a sex or gender item; name the item type and the reporter in notes. Other: any further gender option (non-binary, transgender, another way, self-described). Unknown: prefer not to say, a merged Other/prefer-not-to-say code, and codes no source document defines. A code merging Female with Other or unknown maps to Female (proximate; name the merge). Carry across waves by the carry-forward rule in the harmonisation guide.

label: Country
description: Participant's location at observation point
allowed_values: Albania|Algeria|Argentina|Armenia|Australia|Austria|Azerbaijan|Belarus|Belgium|Bosnia and Herzegovina|Brazil|Brunei Darussalam|Bulgaria|Cambodia|Canada|Chile|China|Colombia|Costa Rica|Croatia|Cyprus|Czech Republic|Denmark|Dominican Republic|Ecuador|El Salvador|England|Estonia|Faroe Islands|Finland|France|Georgia|Germany|Greece|Greenland|Guatemala|Hong Kong|Hungary|Iceland|India|Indonesia|Iraq|Ireland|Isle of Man|Israel|Italy|Jamaica|Japan|Jordan|Kazakhstan|Kenya|Kosovo|Kyrgyzstan|Latvia|Lebanon|Liechtenstein|Lithuania|Luxembourg|Macao|Macedonia|Malaysia|Malta|Mauritius|Mexico|Monaco|Mongolia|Montenegro|Morocco|Netherlands|New Zealand|Northern Ireland|Norway|Palestine|Panama|Paraguay|Peru|Philippines|Poland|Portugal|Qatar|Republic of Moldova|Romania|Russia|Rwanda|Saudi Arabia|Scotland|Serbia|Singapore|Slovakia|Slovenia|South Africa|South Korea|Spain|Sweden|Switzerland|Taiwan|Tajikistan|Thailand|Trinidad and Tobago|Tunisia|Turkey|Ukraine|United Arab Emirates|United Kingdom|Uruguay|USA|Uzbekistan|Vietnam|Wales|Zambia|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: UK: England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland wherever the data identify the nation; United Kingdom only where they do not. Sub-national samples and separately sampled territories map to their country, named in notes; Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan are values in their own right. No country variable: a constant for where data were collected, inferred, source in notes. Never emit a value missing from allowed_values; ask for it to be added.

label: Australian State
description: Australian state or territory where the participant was observed
missing_rule: Use NA if not applicable (i.e., not an Australian dataset) and Unknown if cannot be derived.
notes: Australian samples only; other datasets are unavailable ('Not an Australian dataset.'). Multi-country datasets: NA for non-Australian rows; Unknown for Australian rows whose state cannot be derived. Name the source (stratum, site, protocol) in notes. Used to report state-relevant findings to NSW DoE.

label: Ethnicity
description: Participant ethnic or racial group, collapsed to the schema categories
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map through the shared ethnicity lookup; resolve released 'other, specify' text through a dataset lookup. US: Hispanic origin first, then race alone; two or more races = Mixed; AI/AN and NHPI = Other. A Hispanic-origin item sets Hispanic only in US and Canadian samples; elsewhere use the race, colour or ethnic-group item. Parda, Coloured and mixed-parentage groups = Mixed. Groups with no schema category (Indigenous and Pacific peoples, Arab/Middle Eastern, Gypsy/Roma/Traveller) = Other (proximate). A parent's own ethnicity used for the child: proximate. No item: unavailable; birthplace, language or religion only: incompatible; never a constant from study context.

label: Participant indigenous status
description: Participant is Indigenous to the country of data collection, as reported by the participant or a parent
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Indigenous: the source's explicit Indigenous category (US American Indian/Alaska Native alone; Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander; First Nations, Métis, Inuit; Māori; indígena). Groups Indigenous elsewhere (Pacific peoples in New Zealand) are Non-Indigenous. Non-Indigenous: any other answer to an item that offered an Indigenous option. Unknown: non-response, and sites whose item offered none. An item that forces multi-heritage respondents to one group outside Indigenous: partial. No Indigenous option in the study: unavailable.

label: Minority
description: Participant belongs to an ethnic minority group relative to the national majority of the country of data collection
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Non-minority: the national majority group (US non-Hispanic White; UK, Canada, Australia any White group; New Zealand European; China Han; elsewhere the numerical majority). All other groups, including Mixed and Hispanic, are Minority. Use the same item, free-text resolution and carry-forward as ethnicity. No ethnicity item: First- or Second-generation immigrant_background -> Minority, Native -> Non-minority (proximate); with parents' birthplaces only, both parents abroad (or one abroad and the other unknown) -> Minority, at least one born in the country -> Non-minority, otherwise Unknown (proximate); a direct item on membership of an ethnic or discriminated-against minority: proximate. No numerical majority (e.g. Brazil) or religion only: incompatible; Unknown for such sites in multi-country data.

label: Immigrant background
description: Immigrant background of the participant, from the birthplace of the participant and their parents
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Native: at least one parent born in the country of data collection. Second-generation: participant born in the country, both parents abroad. First-generation: participant and both parents abroad. One parent's birthplace unknown: the other decides. Unknown: no parent's birthplace known, or no parent born in the country and the participant's birthplace unknown. Use the UK as a whole; Hong Kong and Macao in their own right. Parents are the mother and father figures the source records; partial when one is systematically unobserved (resident figures only, not interviewed, never asked). Incompatible: child birthplace, language or citizenship alone, or rows that can emit only Native and Unknown.

label: Born in country of data collection
description: Whether the participant was born in the country where the data were collected
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived
notes: From the participant's own birthplace; fill wherever it is recorded, including studies that also map immigrant_background. Use the UK as a whole (born elsewhere in the UK counts as Yes for a sample from one UK nation); Hong Kong and Macao in their own right. A constant Yes is allowed only where recruitment at birth in the country guarantees it (inferred). Carried within participant (carry-forward rule).

label: Area-level SES
description: Socioeconomic status for the area the participant lives
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map a national area-deprivation or area-SES index of the residential small area (e.g. IMD, NZDep) on the index's national quintiles: the two least-deprived quintiles = High, the middle quintile = Medium, the two most-deprived = Low; a source already banded at these points maps directly. An officially designated neighbourhood type with a documented SES gradient may stand in (proximate; Medium not emitted). Settlement size, region, urbanicity and school-level indicators do not map here. Record the index, its release and which end is most deprived.

label: Household-level SES
description: Socioeconomic status of the participant's household or family
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Low/Medium/High = 40/20/40 of the unweighted sample within wave (and within country or site where the measure is country- or site-specific); banded sources by ridit, fixed class schemes by their standard three-way collapse, subjective standing at the labelled anchors (household SES cuts in the harmonisation guide). Prefer, in order: composite SES index, equivalised income or income-to-needs, affluence/asset index, occupational class, subjective standing. Parental education alone and school-level indicators do not map here. Compatible: income, income-to-needs, affluence or composite measure with every level within 10 points of 40/20/40 in every wave; proximate otherwise.

label: Household SES Measure Name
description: Source measure used to derive ses_household
missing_rule: Name the measure on every row of a wave in which ses_household is derived, including rows where ses_household is Unknown; NA in waves where it is not derived
notes: Constant per dataset and wave, written '<type>: <measure>', type one of Income | Income-to-needs | Affluence/assets | Composite SES index | Occupational class | Subjective standing (e.g. 'Income: gross annual household income, 13 bands'). Status inferred. The cut rule goes in ses_household notes, not here.

label: Household registration status (hukou)
description: China-specific household registration category, which governs access to schooling and welfare independently of income or current residence
missing_rule: Use NA outside mainland China and wherever hukou was not asked (row unavailable), including China sites of multinational studies; use Unknown only when hukou was asked but the answer cannot be classified, including non-Chinese nationals
notes: Country-specific stratifier; NA for datasets outside mainland China. 'Residence' is the unified category created by the post-2014 hukou reform.

label: Mother's education level
description: Highest completed education of the child's mother
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Mother figure the source identifies (biological, adoptive, step or foster; resident only where the source restricts to residents); name the definition in notes. Secondary school or less = ISCED 0-3, including A-levels, upper-secondary vocational qualifications and apprenticeships. Post-secondary = ISCED 4-5 and tertiary study begun but not completed. Bachelor degree or higher = ISCED 6-8. A source band spanning two levels goes to the level holding most of its members (proximate). Don't know, not applicable, other or foreign qualifications and no-mother codes = Unknown. Map through the shared education lookup.

label: Father's education level
description: Highest completed education of the child's father
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Father figure the source identifies, defined as for maternal_education. Never substitute a non-parent carer; where the source does not say which carer is the father and one is inferred, proximate. Levels and rules as maternal_education.

label: Highest parental education level
description: Highest education level across the child's parents/carers
allowed_values: Secondary school or less|Post-secondary|Bachelor degree or higher|Unknown
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Highest level across the parents or carers the source records, resident non-parent carers included. Use the study's own highest-parent variable when one exists. Otherwise take the maximum of the ordered source codes after dropping don't-know and not-applicable codes, so one known parent suffices. In waves where only one parent was asked about, emit Unknown. Levels and rules as maternal_education.

label: Urbanicity
description: Urban, suburban or rural character of the participant's area of residence
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Map an official national urban/rural typology by its own levels, in order, keeping its own thresholds. Raw settlement-size bands: under 5,000 inhabitants = Rural, 5,000 to under 100,000 = Suburban, 100,000 or more = Urban; a band straddling a threshold goes where most of its population lies. Binary sources emit Urban and Rural only. School location or a sampling stratum may stand in for residence. A study-level constant (inferred) only when the design guarantees urban residence at the measured wave. Compatible only for a residential three-level typology; proximate otherwise.

label: Family structure
description: Family structure of the household the child lives in (main home where the child has more than one)
missing_rule: Use Unknown if cannot be derived, including waves where the item was not asked and no value is carried; never NA on a mapped row
notes: Two biological/adoptive parents: both resident parental figures are biological or adoptive, even if a step-parent is also reported. Step family: two resident parental figures, at least one biological/adoptive and at least one step-parent or a parent's co-resident partner. Single parent: one resident parental figure, no co-resident partner. Other: no resident biological/adoptive parent (grandparent, foster or institutional care, step-parent only). Shared care: the main home; none identifiable = Unknown. Source cannot separate step-parents from parents: use the category its structure forces (never Unknown for one category only), name it, proximate.

label: Family: Parental rules on screen time
description: Whether parents set rules limiting how much or when the child uses screens
notes: TRUE if any rule limits the amount or timing of screen use; content-only rules are FALSE. Where asked per device, TRUE if any device has such a rule. Record the respondent and devices covered. A parent's technical time limit (device or app settings) is partial.

label: Family: Screen device in bedroom
description: Whether a screen device (TV, computer, games console, tablet or phone) is kept in the child's bedroom
notes: TRUE if any covered device is in the bedroom. Record the devices the item covers; an item on one device only (e.g. a TV) is partial. A behaviour item that places a device in the bedroom (using it there, keeping it by the bed at night) is partial, TRUE for any use or occurrence.

label: Family: Parenting stress
description: Total score on the study's parenting-stress scale, where higher indicates more stress
notes: Generic row for parenting-stress scales (e.g. the Parenting Stress Index short form total or one of its subscales). Record the instrument and subscales in fam_parentstress_measure; standardise within dataset at analysis.

label: Family: Parenting stress measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind fam_parentstress
missing_rule: Should not be missing where fam_parentstress is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument and subscales>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>'. Status inferred.

label: School grade or year level
description: School grade or year level at the observation
notes: The study's own year-level label, translated where needed but keeping system terms (Year 7, Klasse 5, 9th year ensino fundamental, 3ro ESO, Junior high 2); never renumber onto another system. One wording per school system across datasets (Korea: 'Middle School 1st Grade'). Grade fixed by sampling whole classes of one grade: emit it, compatible. Grade deduced from cohort progression or birth-date windows: inferred, and only where documentation names the grade. School-type or sampled age-group codes without a year level: incompatible. For sample description only.

label: Screen Time Measure ID
description: Identifies which screen-time measure a row carries when a dataset contributes more than one (for example a questionnaire and a time-use diary, or a parent and a child report). The rows derived from a datasets untagged variables.csv mapping are primary; rows produced by a measure tag in variables.csv carry that tag. participant_id + wave + st_measure_id identify a row.
missing_rule: Injected by the harmoniser, should never be missing
notes: System variable filled by the pipeline, not mapped in variables.csv. Filtering to st_measure_id == primary reproduces the one-row-per-participant-wave table.

label: Screen Time Measurement Type
description: Response format of the screen-time items on this row
notes: Continuous: open numeric time entry (hours or minutes), time-use diary or device log. Categorical: response bands, including bands the study or the mapping scores as hours. Where items of both formats feed a row, record the format behind its core st_ variables and name the other in notes. Vary by wave where the format changes.

label: Screen Time Measure Name
description: Instrument that supplied the screen-time items on this row
missing_rule: Should not be missing; use "Unknown" only when item provenance cannot be established
notes: One controlled label: the published name of a standalone instrument (e.g. "Questionnaire for Screen Time of Adolescents (QueST)"); "Time use diary" for diaries; "Custom" for items written for the study or its survey programme, including the study's own questionnaire; "Unknown" only when item provenance cannot be established. Never combined labels ("Unknown/custom") or "Custom: ..." variants. Item wording, codes and waves go in variables.csv notes.

label: Screen Time Respondent
description: Who reported the screen-time values on this row
allowed_values: Self|Parent or carer|Teacher|Device or objective measure|Other|Unknown
missing_rule: NA on rows with no screen-time value; Unknown when the row has screen-time values but the respondent cannot be determined
notes: One responder per row: every st_ value on the row, and every filter question that sets one to zero, comes from that responder. Vary by wave or age where the respondent changes by design; with no who-answered variable, deduce it from which item series is answered and record the cut in notes. Primary rows carry the study's main series; a second responder on the same occasion is a tagged measure block (DR-0003). Never combine responders within a row or a variable.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average weekday
description: Total time engaging in screen use on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_total; rules as st_total.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average weekend day
description: Total time engaging in screen use on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_total; rules as st_total.

label: Screen Time: Aggregated total on average day
description: Total time engaging in screen use on a regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Not for the original IPD. Map one item on all screen use, or sum items the instrument defines as mutually exclusive parts of it (contexts such as location, learning vs leisure, alone vs co-use). Partial if devices or purposes are excluded. A sum of separately asked activity or device items is incompatible, including a total the study computed from them (DR-0002, DR-0004). Internet-only and single-device items go to their own rows and are incompatible here. A skipped part leaves a summed total NA; never score it as zero unless the instrument's documentation does.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on average weekday
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_watch; rules as st_watch.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on average weekend day
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_watch; rules as st_watch.

label: Screen Time: Watching (e.g., TV, streaming) on usual day
description: Time spent watching content (e.g., TV, movies, streaming) on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: TV, films, series and online video on any device. Partial: an item limited to the TV set (broadcast TV, videos or DVDs on the set), or one that also counts gaming at the TV or radio. Viewing sources (broadcast, DVD, streaming, online video) may be summed here (DR-0002); record the sum. An item pooling watching with gaming, computer or internet use goes to st_total.

label: Screen Time: Gaming (any device) on average weekday
description: Time spent playing video games on any device (console, computer, handheld, phone, tablet) on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game; rules as st_game.

label: Screen Time: Gaming (any device) on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing video games on any device (console, computer, handheld, phone, tablet) on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game; rules as st_game.

label: Screen Time: Gaming (any device) on usual day
description: Time spent playing video games on any device (console, computer, handheld, phone, tablet) on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Device-specific gaming items may be summed here (DR-0002); record the sum. An item pooling gaming with other non-school computer use maps here as partial, and st_comp* is incompatible. An item whose examples name social media is not mapped here (incompatible). An item naming devices that leaves out phones and tablets (e.g. computer or console) is partial whatever its year; an item naming no device is compatible.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_comp; rules as st_game_comp.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_comp; rules as st_game_comp.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on computer on usual day
description: Time spent playing games on a computer on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Computer gaming only. Computer and tablet offered as one response option go to st_game_tablet (partial); this row is then incompatible. Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_console; rules as st_game_console.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_console; rules as st_game_console.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a regular console on usual day
description: Time spent playing games on a regular console on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Console gaming only. A console item that also covers handhelds maps here as partial, and st_game_handheldconsole is incompatible. Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a handheld console on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a handheld console on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_handheldconsole; rules as st_game_handheldconsole.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a handheld console on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing games on a handheld console on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_handheldconsole; rules as st_game_handheldconsole.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a handheld console on usual day
description: Time spent playing games on a handheld console on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Handheld-console gaming only. A console item that also covers handhelds goes to st_game_console (partial); this row is then incompatible. Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming using active-gaming equipment on average weekday
description: Time spent playing active games on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_active; rules as st_game_active.

label: Screen Time: Gaming using active-gaming equipment on average weekend day
description: Time spent playing active games on weekends
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekend or non-school-day variant of st_game_active; rules as st_game_active.

label: Screen Time: Gaming using active-gaming equipment on usual day
description: Time spent playing active games on regular or average day
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Under a pooled multi-device gaming item this row is unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.').

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a phone on average weekday
description: Time spent playing games on a phone on weekdays
missing_rule: Use NA if not asked or not answered; use 0 where a filter establishes non-use (non-users rule in the harmonisation guide)
notes: Weekday or school-day variant of st_game_phone; rules as st_game_phone.

label: Screen Time: Gaming on a phone on average weekend day

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - self-rated
description: Child-reported rating of their overall school performance, grades or class standing (their own view, or their teacher's view as they perceive it)
notes: The HBSC item (what the teacher thinks of the child's performance compared with classmates) or the child's own rating of overall grades or class standing. Five-level scales: the five-level collapse in the harmonisation guide (proximate). Letter or numeric grades go to acc_academachment_lettergrades or acc_academachment_numgrades; satisfaction with performance to wb_domainsat_schoolwork_self. Quality-of-life school items (e.g. KIDSCREEN), subject self-concept items ('I am good at maths') and parent ratings are incompatible.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - student grades (categorical letter grades)
description: Overall school grade reported as a letter grade
missing_rule: Use NA if not available; 'not graded', 'not sure' and pass/fail are NA
notes: Overall grade only; grades for single subjects are incompatible. Fold +/- onto the letter (proximate); 'Mostly X's' = X; a two-letter band = X/Y; an open bottom band ('D or lower') = D. Also map every letter-grade source to acc_academachment_numgrades, and never pool the two rows as independent outcomes.

label: Academic Achievement: General education - standardised tests
description: Score on a standardised general-education achievement test: an overall composite, or a subject other than reading and mathematics (e.g. science)
notes: Reading and mathematics tests go to acc_literacy_stdtest or acc_numeracy_stdtest, never here. Map one test per dataset (the one fielded in most waves) and record the test, domain and score type.

label: Academic Engagement: Cares about doing well in school
description: How often the child cares about doing well in school
notes: Frequency ratings only ('All/Most/Some of the time' = Always/Usually/Sometimes). Degree, importance or agreement ratings, effort items ('tries their best') and liking or enjoying school are incompatible. Record the informant and waves.

label: Academic Engagement: Completes all required homework
description: How often the child does all the homework they are required to do
notes: Completion-frequency items only. Homework hours, how often homework is set, parental checking, and difficulty or lateness items are incompatible. Record the informant and waves.

label: Academic: Pressure from schoolwork (self-report)
description: How pressured the participant feels by the schoolwork they have to do
notes: Single item. Scales with other anchors map by rank and are proximate; record the anchors. A five-point pressure scale maps its top two levels to 'A lot'. Worry about school performance and test anxiety are related items (incompatible, item named).

label: Academic: School belonging (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's school belonging or connectedness scale, where higher indicates stronger belonging
notes: Generic row for multi-item belonging or connectedness scales. Reverse negatively worded items so higher = stronger belonging; record the instrument and scoring in acc_schoolbelonging_measure; standardise within dataset. Single items are incompatible; satisfaction with school goes to wb_domainsat_school_self. Only scales presented as belonging or connectedness; teacher- or classmate-support scales and school-environment quality-of-life subscales are incompatible.

label: Academic: School belonging measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind acc_schoolbelonging_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where acc_schoolbelonging_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items. Status inferred.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - student grades (numeric)
description: Overall school grades on a numeric scale (grade points, percentage or national scale), including US letter grades converted to grade points, where higher indicates better achievement
notes: Reverse scales where a low mark is best (German 1-6: 7 - mark). US letter grades: A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0, +/- = ±0.3, two-letter bands at their midpoint, 'D or lower' = 1; one overall grade compatible, bands partial. Subject marks only: mean of all academic subjects reported (not arts, PE or ICT), all required, partial. Never convert between national scales; record the source metric.

label: Academic Achievement: Academic Achievement - teacher-rated

notes: Teacher's overall rating, or the mean of the teacher's ratings of every academic subject rated (language, maths, science or social studies; not arts, PE or ICT), all required, partial; round half toward the poorer level. Five-level scales: the five-level collapse in the harmonisation guide. A student's report of the teacher's view goes to acc_academachment_selfrated.

notes: Record the test and score type in variables.csv; standardise within dataset and wave at analysis

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Engaged in bullying other students
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports bullying other students during the study's recall period
notes: Bullying other students, in person or in a mode the item leaves open; where the study asks the mode, use the in-person answer. Online-only items go to beh_bullied_online. Compatible: a global bullying item or a multi-type perpetration checklist. Partial: hurtful acts not framed as bullying, a target wider than peers, or parent report. Truth-rated items (SDQ item 12, CBCL) are incompatible; name the item.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied by other students
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being bullied by other students during the study's recall period
notes: Compatible: a global bullying item, or any item of a multi-type peer-victimisation checklist (hit, threatened, teased, left out, rumours, belongings taken or damaged, extortion). Online-only items go to beh_beenbullied_online and stay out of the checklist; where the study asks the mode, use the in-person answer. Partial: hurtful acts not framed as bullying, any perpetrator rather than peers, or parent report. Truth-rated items (SDQ item 19, CBCL) are incompatible; name the item.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied online by others
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being bullied online
notes: Online or electronic bullying by anyone; peer-only items are compatible. Compatible: a global cyberbullying item or a multi-type checklist of cyberbullying acts (abuse, rumours, exclusion, exposing personal information, threats, extortion). Partial: an item on one act type, or a single hostile or humiliating experience not framed as bullying.

label: Behaviour: Bullying - Bullied others online
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports bullying others online during the study's recall period
notes: Online or electronic bullying of anyone. Compatible: a global item or a multi-type checklist of cyberbullying acts. Partial: an item on one act type, or hostile acts not framed as bullying.

label: Behaviour: Fighting - Engaged in fighting
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports being in a physical fight during the study's recall period
notes: Partial: an item limited to one setting (school property; school or work) or form (group fights), or one counting any push or hit. Truth-rated items ('I fight a lot', SDQ 12, CBCL 'gets in many fights') are incompatible.

label: Behaviour: Truancy - Missed school without permission
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports missing school without permission during the study's recall period
notes: Unexcused absence from school or classes (truancy, skipping, cutting), whole or part days; whole-day-only items are compatible. Absence through illness or with permission does not count. TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period. NA for respondents not enrolled in school.

label: Behaviour: Stealing - Took money or property without permission
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports stealing money or property during the study's recall period
notes: Theft of money or property: shoplifting; theft from a person, home, school or vehicle; vehicle theft; burglary; card use without permission. Shoplifting only: partial. Not here: extortion (bullying rows), fare evasion, driving without permission, steal-or-damage items, truth-rated SDQ items. TRUE at any occurrence; record each wave's items and recall period.

label: Behaviour: Vandalism - Deliberately damaged property
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports deliberately damaging or destroying property that was not theirs during the study's recall period
notes: Deliberate damage to others' property: breaking, graffiti, setting fire to property. One setting only (school property): partial. Not here: fire-setting with no property named, neighbourhood vandalism. TRUE at any occurrence; record each wave's items and recall period.

label: Behaviour: Alcohol use (self-report)

notes: Any drinking; items on drunkenness or binge drinking only are partial. TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period (past 30 days preferred). Lifetime items are partial.

label: Behaviour: Tobacco use (self-report)

label: Behaviour: Cannabis use (self-report)
description: Binary where TRUE means the participant reports using cannabis during the study's recall period
notes: TRUE for any occurrence; record the recall period. Lifetime items are partial; items pooling cannabis with other drugs are partial.

Scale totals stay in their score rows and are incompatible here, as are mood-frequency items (mh_sad_self, HBSC-SCL); name the item. Not a diagnosis: do not pool with mh_dep_diagnosed. Recall other than 12 months is partial; record the item wording and the recall period.

label: Mental Health: Depression - depression scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's multi-item self-report depression scale, where higher indicates more depressive symptoms
notes: When a named depression row is mapped, repeat its expression here unchanged. Short, adapted and study-specific forms go here and not to a named row (mh_dep_scl_self also takes SCL-90-R short forms); compatible when mh_dep_measure describes them. Single items go to mh_sad_self or mh_dep_binary_self; this row is then incompatible, naming them.

label: Mental Health: Depression measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind mh_dep_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where mh_dep_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Mental Health: Anxiety - anxiety scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's multi-item self-report anxiety scale, where higher indicates more anxiety
notes: When a named anxiety row is mapped, repeat its expression here unchanged. Short, adapted and study-specific forms go here and not to a named row; compatible when mh_anx_measure describes them. Single items go to their single-item row where one fits (e.g. mh_worry_self); this row is then incompatible, naming them.

label: Mental Health: Anxiety measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind mh_anx_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where mh_anx_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>)', then the reverse-scored items and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Mental Health: Depression or anxiety - diagnosed
description: Whether a health professional has ever told the respondent the child has depression or anxiety, and whether the child currently has them
notes: One item naming depression and anxiety together maps here, and mh_dep_diagnosed and mh_anx_diagnosed are incompatible; separate items: the reverse. Never = never told; Previously = told, not current; Currently = told and current. Treatment or medication as proxy for current: partial. Not attributed to a health professional: incompatible. Not a symptom score; record the informant.

label: Mental Health: Perceived stress - self-report
description: Self-reported amount of stress the participant usually feels, on a single item
allowed_values: A great deal|A lot|Some|A little|None at all
notes: Map anchors by wording; a rank-order mapping whose anchors differ from these labels is proximate. Worry frequencies (mh_worry_self), schoolwork-pressure items and pooled distress items (depressed, anxious or stressed) are incompatible here; name the item. Stress scales need a score row. A parent's own stress is unavailable.

label: Mental Health: Loneliness - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling lonely over the study's recall period
notes: Direct 'lonely' wording only. Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). Indirect items (isolated, left out, lack companionship) and intensity or distress ratings of loneliness are incompatible; multi-item scales go to mh_lonely_scale_self.

label: Mental Health: Loneliness - loneliness scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's self-reported loneliness scale, where higher indicates more loneliness
notes: Any multi-item loneliness scale (UCLA or a short form, or a study item set). Sum with positively worded items reversed; confirm each reversal against the item-rest correlation, since some sources store these items already reversed. List the items in mh_lonely_measure. Single items go to mh_lonely_self; a study may populate both.

label: Mental Health: Loneliness measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind mh_lonely_scale_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where mh_lonely_scale_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>)', then the reverse-scored items and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Mental Health: Sadness - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling sad over the study's recall period
notes: Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). HBSC-SCL 'feeling low' goes to wb_psychcomplaints_feellow and yes/no two-week sad-or-hopeless screens to mh_dep_binary_self; where only such an item exists, mark this row incompatible and name it.

label: Mental Health: Worry - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling very worried over the study's recall period
notes: Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). Partial: worry without 'very'; GAD-7 item 3 (GAD-7 crosswalk). Incompatible: single-topic worry (money, tests), sleep lost through worry, 'feeling anxious'. HBSC-SCL 'nervous' goes to wb_psychcomplaints_nervous, stress ratings to mh_stress_self. Record what the worry is about.

label: Mental Health: Irritability - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling irritable or bad-tempered over the study's recall period
notes: Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). Anger or temper-loss items and items pooling irritability with nervousness are partial. GAD-7 item 6 maps here as proximate (GAD-7 crosswalk). HBSC-SCL irritability goes to wb_psychcomplaints_irritable.

label: Mental Health: Feeling uncared for - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling that nobody cares about them over the study's recall period
notes: Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). Support-availability items (someone to turn to, someone who shows affection) are incompatible. Loneliness items belong in mh_lonely_self and do not bear on this row.

label: Mental Health: Feeling life is not worth living - self-report
description: Self-reported frequency of feeling that life is not worth living over the study's recall period
notes: Includes wishing to be dead. Frequency-item rules apply (harmonisation guide). 'Life is meaningless' items are incompatible. Yes/no suicidal-ideation items go to mh_suicide_ideation_self; where only such an item exists, mark this row incompatible and name it. Never pool with scale scores.

label: Mental Health: Suicidal ideation - self-report
description: Whether the participant seriously considered suicide during the study's recall period
notes: Dichotomise counts or frequencies to any vs none. Passive death-wish and self-harm items are not ideation; where only such items exist, mark this row incompatible and name them. Distress ratings of thoughts of ending one's life (symptom checklists) are incompatible. Recall other than 12 months is partial; record the recall period.

label: Mental Health: Suicide attempt - self-report
description: Whether the participant attempted suicide during the study's recall period
notes: Dichotomise counts to any vs none. Where the item was skipped because the ideation item was answered No, code the skip as No; other skips are NA. Self-harm or self-inflicted injury items are incompatible. Recall other than 12 months (e.g. lifetime) is partial; record the recall period.

label: Mental Health: Self-harm - self-report
description: Whether the participant reports hurting themselves on purpose during the study's recall period
notes: Any deliberate self-injury, whatever the intent. Suicide attempts go to mh_suicide_attempt_self; a single item pooling both maps here as partial. Record the recall period; lifetime items are partial.

label: Mental Health: Psychosomatic complaints - HBSC symptom checklist total (self-report)
description: Total score on the HBSC symptom checklist (HBSC-SCL) frequency items, where higher indicates more frequent complaints
notes: Sum of the eight HBSC-SCL items (headache, stomach ache, back ache, feeling low, irritability, nervousness, sleep difficulties, dizziness), each 1 rarely or never to 5 about every day, complete-case; reverse sources coded 1 = about every day. Drop extra items. Fewer than eight: incompatible (map the wb_psychcomplaints_* rows). Other checklists: unavailable.

label: Mental Health: Psychosomatic complaints measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind mh_psychsom_hbscscl_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where mh_psychsom_hbscscl_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <recall period>', then any items added or dropped. Status inferred.

label: Mental Health: Somatic complaints - symptom scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the study's somatic or psychosomatic complaints scale, where higher indicates more complaints
notes: Generic row for symptom scales other than the HBSC-SCL, which has its own row (mh_psychsom_hbscscl_self). Record the instrument and scoring in mh_somatic_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Mental Health: Somatic complaints measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind mh_somatic_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where mh_somatic_self is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Emotional Self-control - Behavior Assessment System for Children-2 Emotional Self-control subscale
description: Raw score on the BASC-2 Emotional Self-Control content scale, where higher indicates poorer emotional self-control
notes: Raw sum of the scale's items as keyed in the BASC-2 manual. Raw scores differ by form: record the form and items answered, and standardise within dataset. Check a study-supplied total against the item key before mapping it.

label: Wellbeing: Mental Wellbeing - Warwick Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale
description: Total of the 14 WEMWBS items, 1-5 item scoring (range 14-70)
notes: 14-item form only, complete-case sum. SWEMWBS goes to wb_mwb_swemwbs_self.

label: Wellbeing: Life Satisfaction - Cantril Ladder
description: Cantril ladder rung, 0 (worst possible life) to 10 (best possible life)
notes: Ladder wording only. Other life-satisfaction items, including 0-10 satisfaction scales, go to wb_lifesat_singleitem_self.

label: Wellbeing: Resilience - Behavior Assessment System for Children-2 Resilience subscale
description: Raw score on the BASC-2 Resiliency content scale, where higher indicates greater resilience
notes: Raw sum as keyed in the BASC-2 manual. Record the form and items answered. Before mapping a study-supplied total, check that every item correlates positively with it; a total that adds problem-worded items unreversed is not this variable.

label: Wellbeing: Psychological complaints - Feeling low (HBSC-SCL)
description: How often the participant felt low in the last 6 months (HBSC symptom checklist item)
allowed_values: About every day|More than once a week|About every week|About every month|Rarely or never
notes: HBSC-SCL 'feeling low' item, or its PISA 2018/2022 well-being adaptation ('feeling depressed'), recoded by label. Sad or low-mood items with other wording or response scales are not mapped here (see mh_sad_self). Named-instrument row: unavailable ('HBSC-SCL not administered; see <row>.') wherever neither version was given, even when a related item is in hand.

label: Wellbeing: Psychological complaints - Irritability or bad temper (HBSC-SCL)
description: How often the participant was irritable or bad-tempered in the last 6 months (HBSC symptom checklist item)
allowed_values: About every day|More than once a week|About every week|About every month|Rarely or never
notes: HBSC-SCL 'irritability or bad temper' item, or the identical PISA 2018/2022 well-being item, recoded by label. Other irritability items are not mapped here (see mh_irritable_self). Named-instrument row: unavailable ('HBSC-SCL not administered; see <row>.') wherever neither version was given, even when a related item is in hand.

label: Wellbeing: Psychological complaints - Feeling nervous (HBSC-SCL)
description: How often the participant felt nervous in the last 6 months (HBSC symptom checklist item)
allowed_values: About every day|More than once a week|About every week|About every month|Rarely or never
notes: HBSC-SCL 'feeling nervous' item, or the identical PISA 2018/2022 well-being item, recoded by label. Items with other wording or response scales are not mapped here. Named-instrument row: unavailable ('HBSC-SCL not administered; see <row>.') wherever neither version was given, even when a related item is in hand.

label: Wellbeing: Psychological complaints - Difficulty getting to sleep (HBSC-SCL)
description: How often the participant had difficulty getting to sleep in the last 6 months (HBSC symptom checklist item)
allowed_values: About every day|More than once a week|About every week|About every month|Rarely or never
notes: HBSC-SCL 'difficulty getting to sleep' item, or the identical PISA 2018/2022 well-being item, recoded by label. Sleep duration, sleep latency and nights-per-week items are not mapped here. Named-instrument row: unavailable ('HBSC-SCL not administered; see <row>.') wherever neither version was given, even when a related item is in hand.

label: Wellbeing: Body Image - from HBSC
description: Self-perceived body size, much too thin to much too fat
allowed_values: Much too thin|A bit too thin|About right|A bit too fat|Much too fat
notes: Self-report only. Too-thin/too-fat items map by label; weight-status wording (underweight/overweight) maps by rank and is proximate, and an undegraded 'underweight' maps to A bit too thin. Body or appearance satisfaction goes to wb_domainsat_appearance_self.

label: Wellbeing: Life Satisfaction - Students' Life Satisfaction Scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the 7-item SLSS using 1-6 item scoring
notes: A non-standard response scale (e.g. 4-point) is partial; record it.

label: Wellbeing: Life Satisfaction - Satisfaction With Life Scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the 5-item SWLS using 1-7 item scoring
notes: A non-standard response scale (e.g. 4-point) is partial; record it. The 7-item SLSS goes to wb_lifesat_slss_self.

label: Wellbeing: Life Satisfaction - single item (self-report)
description: Score on a single-item life satisfaction question, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: One general life-satisfaction question other than the Cantril ladder; single happiness ratings go to wb_happiness_singleitem_self. Never use an item scored in a scale mapped on another row for the dataset; an item of an unmapped scale is partial. Where the only such measure is the Cantril ladder or an item of a mapped scale, this row is incompatible; name the item.

label: Wellbeing: Happiness - single item (self-report)
description: Score on a single-item happiness rating, where higher indicates greater happiness
notes: One general happiness question. Reverse scales where the lowest number is the happiest; record the scale points and anchors; standardise within dataset. Life satisfaction goes to wb_lifesat_singleitem_self; items of a scale mapped on another row are not used.

label: Wellbeing: Domain satisfaction - their school work (self-report)
description: Score on a single item rating the participant's satisfaction or happiness with their school work, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: Includes what is learned at school. Satisfaction with performance or grades, or with educational experiences as a whole, is partial. Performance or coping ratings without satisfaction anchors are not mapped. NA for respondents enrolled beyond secondary school.

label: Wellbeing: Domain satisfaction - their appearance (self-report)
description: Score on a single item rating the participant's satisfaction or happiness with their appearance, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: Body-satisfaction items are partial. The too-thin/too-fat item goes to wb_bodyimage.

label: Wellbeing: Domain satisfaction - their family (self-report)
description: Score on a single item rating the participant's satisfaction or happiness with their family, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: Satisfaction with the relationship with parents is partial; where mother and father are asked separately, use the mean of the answered items. Support, parenting-style, fair-treatment and 'fun with' items are incompatible; name the item.

label: Wellbeing: Domain satisfaction - their friends (self-report)
description: Score on a single item rating the participant's satisfaction or happiness with their friends, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: Support and 'fun with friends' items are incompatible; name the item.

label: Wellbeing: Domain satisfaction - the school they go to (self-report)
description: Score on a single item rating the participant's satisfaction or happiness with the school they go to, where higher indicates greater satisfaction
notes: School as a place and school life. Liking, enjoying and happy-at-school items are partial. NA for respondents enrolled beyond secondary school. School work goes to wb_domainsat_schoolwork_self.

label: Wellbeing: Health-related Quality of Life - Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory total score (self-report)
description: Total scale score transformed to 0-100 where higher indicates better quality of life
notes: Generic Core Scales total: items transformed 0-4 -> 100-0 and averaged over answered items (NA if fewer than half are answered). Record the module and age form.

label: Wellbeing: Health-related Quality of Life - Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory total score (parent/carer proxy report)
description: Total scale score transformed to 0-100 where higher indicates better quality of life
notes: Generic Core Scales total: items transformed 0-4 -> 100-0 and averaged over answered items (NA if fewer than half are answered). Record the module and age form.

label: Wellbeing: Health-related Quality of Life - KIDSCREEN-10 (self-report)
description: Sum of the 10 items using 1-5 item scoring
notes: Raw sum with sad and lonely reversed. Recompute from items when the source gives Rasch T-values. Items from a KIDSCREEN-27/52 administration qualify. Non-standard response anchors are partial.

label: Wellbeing: Health-related Quality of Life - KIDSCREEN-10 (parent/carer proxy report)
description: Sum of the 10 items using 1-5 item scoring
notes: Raw sum of the proxy items with sad and lonely reversed. Recompute, or use the released raw sum, when the source gives Rasch T-values.

label: Wellbeing: Self-esteem - Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the 10 items using 1-4 item scoring
notes: Full 10-item scale only; subsets go to wb_selfesteem_self, and this row is then incompatible. A non-standard response scale (e.g. 5-point agreement) is partial. Rescale 0-3 scoring to 1-4.

label: Wellbeing: Self-esteem - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: Total self-esteem score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates greater self-esteem
notes: Any self-esteem scale or item subset. Datasets with the full Rosenberg fill both rows. Score every item asked consistently across waves. Record the measure in wb_selfesteem_measure.

label: Wellbeing: Self-esteem Measure Name
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_selfesteem_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_selfesteem_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Self-efficacy - General Self-Efficacy Scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the 10-item GSE using 1-4 item scoring
notes: Full 10-item GSE only; a non-standard response scale is partial. Subsets go to wb_selfefficacy_self, and this row is then incompatible.

label: Wellbeing: Self-efficacy - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: General self-efficacy total score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates greater self-efficacy
notes: Any general self-efficacy scale or GSE subset. Datasets with the full GSE fill both rows. Domain-specific (academic, physical activity) efficacy and locus-of-control items are not mapped. Record the measure in wb_selfefficacy_measure.

label: Wellbeing: Self-efficacy Measure Name
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_selfefficacy_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_selfefficacy_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Mental Wellbeing - WHO-5 Well-Being Index (self-report)
description: Raw total score using 0-5 item scoring
notes: Record the raw 0-25 score, not the 0-100 percentage transformation

label: Wellbeing: Subjective Happiness - Subjective Happiness Scale (self-report)
description: Total score on the 4-item SHS with the fourth item reverse-scored, where higher indicates greater happiness
notes: Standard 1-7 item scoring (range 4-28); a non-standard response scale is partial. Record whether the mapped value is a sum or a mean item score.

label: Wellbeing: Mental Wellbeing - Short Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale (self-report)
description: Metric score on the 7-item SWEMWBS
notes: Published metric score. Convert a raw 7-item sum with the published conversion table. The 7 items scored from a WEMWBS-14 administration qualify. Record whether the score was released or converted.

label: Wellbeing: Self-rated general health
description: Participant's rating of their own general health
notes: Self-report only; proxy ratings and ratings relative to peers are not mapped. Four-level excellent/good/fair/poor maps by label, leaving Very good unused. Symmetric five-level scales (very good-very poor, or centred on average) map by rank and are proximate.

label: Wellbeing: Parent-rated child general health
description: Parent or carer's rating of the child's general health
notes: Proxy counterpart of wb_selfratedhealth_self; the same recode rules apply.

label: Wellbeing: Positive affect - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: Total positive affect score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates more frequent positive feelings
notes: Published positive-affect scale or subscale (e.g. PISA 2018 positive affect, PANAS-C PA), even if it shares an item with another mapped scale. Single mood items and ad hoc sums of another instrument's items are not mapped. Record the measure in wb_posaffect_measure.

label: Wellbeing: Positive affect measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_posaffect_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_posaffect_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Eudaimonic wellbeing - total score (self-report, any instrument)
description: Total eudaimonic wellbeing score as scored by the source study, where higher indicates greater eudaimonic wellbeing
notes: Multi-item eudaimonic scale scored as a whole: purpose, meaning, self-realisation, effortful engagement (e.g. QEWB, Flourishing Scale, PISA meaning in life). Single items, grit, EPOCH subscales and parent-rated flourishing are not mapped. Do not pool with WEMWBS, SWEMWBS or WHO-5. Record the measure in wb_eudaimonic_measure.

label: Wellbeing: Eudaimonic wellbeing measure
description: Source measure, item count and item scoring behind wb_eudaimonic_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where wb_eudaimonic_self is non-missing; NA in waves or country-cycles where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>, <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>', then the reverse-scored items (or 'supplied already keyed') and any change of response format or recall period from the published form. Status inferred.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived support from family (self-report)
description: Score on the study's scale of perceived social support from family, where higher indicates more support
notes: Generic row for family-support scales or subscales (e.g. the MSPSS family subscale). Only items on support the child receives or can call on (help, understanding, someone to talk to or confide in). Parenting behaviours, family involvement (talk, meals, interest in schoolwork), parenting-style and monitoring items are incompatible. A published support subscale that mixes in companionship items is partial. Record the instrument and scoring of both support rows in wb_socsupport_measure; standardise within dataset.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived support from friends (self-report)
description: Score on the study's scale of perceived social support from friends, where higher indicates more support
notes: Generic row for friend-support scales or subscales (e.g. the MSPSS friends subscale); item scope as wb_socsupport_family_self. Companionship items (time or fun with friends) are not support; a subscale mixing them in is partial. Counts of friends are incompatible.

label: Wellbeing: Perceived social support measure
description: Source measure, item counts and item scoring behind wb_socsupport_family_self and wb_socsupport_friends_self
missing_rule: Should not be missing where either support score is non-missing; NA in waves where the scales were not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument>; family: <k> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>; friends: ...'. Status inferred.

label: Health: Sleep duration on weekdays
description: Usual sleep duration on school nights or weekdays
notes: Hours asleep. Time of falling or going to sleep to waking is compatible (unless banded); bedtime or lights-out to waking is partial; never subtract a separate sleep-latency item. An open band takes the bound its label states, or half an hour beyond a neighbouring point label ('less than 6 hours' next to '6 hours' = 5.5); the share in an open band does not lower the status. Keep durations under 4 or over 16 hours; they are screened at analysis. Record the respondent.

label: Health: Sleep duration on weekends
description: Usual sleep duration on weekend or non-school nights
notes: As hlth_sleep_wd.

label: Health: Sleep duration on an average night
description: Usual sleep duration on an average night
notes: 5:2 weighted mean of hlth_sleep_wd and hlth_sleep_we where both exist; otherwise a usual-night item. As hlth_sleep_wd for clock times, bands and implausible values.

label: Health: Sleep problems score
description: Total score on the study's sleep-problems scale, where higher indicates more problems
notes: Generic row for multi-item sleep-problem scales (e.g. the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children). Record the instrument and respondent in hlth_sleepprob_measure; standardise within dataset. Single items are incompatible; the HBSC-SCL sleep item stays on wb_psychcomplaints_diffsleep.

label: Health: Sleep problems measure
description: Source measure, respondent, item count and item scoring behind hlth_sleepprob
missing_rule: Should not be missing where hlth_sleepprob is non-missing; NA in waves where the scale was not administered; 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified
notes: '<instrument> (<self|parent> report), <k> of <K> items, <a>-<b> item scoring (range <min>-<max>), <sum|mean>'. Status inferred.
